# Cover spec — *Compression Is the Through-Line* (Lulu 6×9 hardcover case-wrap)

Interior: `interior.pdf`, **108 pages**, 6×9 in trim, black-and-white.

## Canvas dimensions

Lulu case-wrap covers are a single flat image: back cover + spine + front cover,
plus a wrap allowance that folds around the boards.

**Spine width** (Lulu standard 60# / ~148 gsm B&W paper):

```
spine = pageCount × 0.0025 in + 0.06 in
      = 108 × 0.0025 + 0.06
      = 0.33 in
```

**Flat cover canvas** (wrap ≈ 0.75 in per edge for case-wrap):

```
width  = wrap + trimWidth + spine + trimWidth + wrap
       = 0.75 + 6 + 0.33 + 6 + 0.75      = 13.83 in
height = wrap + trimHeight + wrap
       = 0.75 + 9 + 0.75                 = 10.5 in
```

At 300 dpi: **4149 × 3150 px**.

> ⚠️ Confirm all of the above against **Lulu's cover calculator / downloadable
> template at upload time** (Lulu generates an exact template PDF for the chosen
> product + page count + paper). The spine formula and wrap allowance here are
> the working assumption, not verified against Lulu's current spec. Keep text
> at least 0.5 in away from the spine folds and wrap edges.

## Front cover copy

- **Title:** Compression Is the Through-Line
- **Subtitle:** Frameworks for Seeing One Pattern Everywhere
- **Author:** Dom Sadarangani

Suggested treatment: match the interior/web aesthetic — near-black field
(`#05060e`), pale ink (`#e8ecff`), a violet accent (`#7c5cff`), serif title,
small mono label for the subtitle. Decorative field of faint stars (the
Constellation motif) is on-brand; no other imagery needed.

## Spine copy

- `COMPRESSION IS THE THROUGH-LINE · DOM SADARANGANI`
- 0.33 in is enough for one line of small type; confirm fit on Lulu's template.

## Back cover copy (~120 words, drawn from the book's own material)

> A second brain is two things wearing one coat: the content — your actual
> notes — and the engine that connects them. This book is what the engine
> surfaced. Fifty-one frameworks and one thesis, genericized from a single
> working vault, all circling the same idea: intelligence and memory are both
> the art of packing more meaning into denser, retrievable representations.
> Learning is compression. The same kernel shows up in language models and
> leadership, in backtests and 1:1s, in Goodhart's law and go-to-market. Each
> chapter is short: the connection, why it matters, and what to do about it.
> Compiled from the Domvault Constellation — an opt-in, credited knowledge
> graph. The thinking is Dom's; the drafting was AI-assisted.

Below the blurb, small mono type:

```
dys5315.github.io/domvault/constellation
PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0
```

(No ISBN barcode is assumed; if Lulu assigns one, leave the standard 2×1.2 in
clear zone in the lower-right of the back cover.)
